exposure: IUD insertion timing (non-post-partum vs. various post-partum intervals)
breastfeeding status at the time of IUD insertion
cohort: The study included 326,658 individuals aged 50 years or younger who had an IUD inserted between Jan 1, 2001, and April 30, 2018, across multiple US healthcare systems.
finding: IUD insertion during the post-partum period, particularly 4 days to 6 weeks or less post partum, was associated with a nearly seven-fold increased risk of uterine perforation compared to non-post-partum insertion, and breastfeeding at insertion also slightly increased this risk.
